subject: Proposal: Shift Burst Credits to Recurring Monthly Commit + Tiered Ops
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Tran <sophie.tran@cartwise.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Shift Burst Credits to Recurring Monthly Commit + Tiered Ops

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a clean proposal that converts your existing burst bucket into a recurring monthly commit, plus a small restructuring of rate bands so you have clearer economics at scale. High level: 

- Convert your current 1.2M monthly burst credits into a 900k/month committed baseline for the next 12 months (commits billed monthly).
- Add a 2-tier rate lattice: up to 1M tokens/month at $0.0009/token, then 1M–5M at $0.0006/token.
- Include a 3-month introductory uplift discount (20% off the baseline rate) to reduce ramp risk.
- Soft-throttle protection and a 10% monthly rollover for unused commit in Q1 to smooth spikes.

I've attached a pricing workbook (hosted_recurring_pricing_v2.xlsx) and a draft mutual action plan that lays out procurement and cutover milestones (CTW_mutual_action_plan.docx). If this looks good, we can route the DocuSign for the amendment and schedule a kickoff with our Onboarding & Ops team next week.

Three asks from our side to make the change low friction: 
1) A short confirmation that Cartwise can commit to the 12-month baseline (we can phase increases if helpful).
2) PO or e-invoice instructions so we align the billing cadence.
3) A two-hour ops kickoff (we'll run inventory of endpoints, SLO mapping, and caching rules).

If you'd like, I can put together a short slide summarizing the economics for your finance team.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Proposal: Shift Burst Credits to Recurring Monthly Commit + Tiered Ops

Hi Ben —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the workbook — thanks. A couple of quick things from finance/ops POV before we expedite: 

1) Overcommit risk: our Legal/Finance are worried about being locked into a baseline if we have a soft quarter. Is there a built-in pause/step-down mechanism if monthly usage drops >40% for two consecutive months?

2) Rollover mechanics: you mentioned 10% monthly rollover for Q1 — can that be extended to a 60-day window instead of month-by-month reconciliation? That helps us plan seasonal spikes.

3) Instrumentation & SLOs: our infra team needs to confirm latency targets for the second-tier rate (1M–5M) — what SLAs will apply and what the failover behavior is if we hit capacity?

Assuming we can land reasonable language on (1) and (2), Marco and I are comfortable moving to a DocuSign. Also — can you provide a short example invoice for Month 1 showing the introductory discount and how overage/rollover posts?

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Tran | Head of Platform
Cartwise

Hi Sophie —

Looping in a quick operational note and an accommodation from our side. We hear the overcommit concern and can offer the following guardrails to de-risk for Cartwise: 

- Step-down protection: If committed usage drops >40% for two consecutive months, we'll automatically reduce the baseline by 25% for a single-month trial (noted as a one-time de-escalation), with the option to revisit at the quarterly review. This is easier operationally than a full pause clause and preserves pool stability.

- Rollover window: we'll change the monthly 10% rule to a 60-day buffer — unused commit can be consumed within 60 days. Any remaining credits after 60 days expire.

- SLA & capacity: the 2-tier rate will carry a target p95 token latency of <120ms for the baseline tier and <190ms for the higher-volume tier. In the event of regional capacity constraints we'll route to a compatible scaled variant with an automatic throttled fallback (we'll notify and open an incident). These behaviors and expected latency ranges will be captured in the amendment.

Financials: Ben — please attach the sample invoice for Month 1 with the initial 20% uplift discount called out and a line for "Introductory promo credit" so Cartwise finance has a clear PO reference. For procurement: we can accept standard PO + Net30 or a signed amendment + e-invoice.

If Sophie/Marco are ok with this language, I propose we route the DocuSign and schedule a Tuesday ops kickoff (45–90 minutes). I'll have our Onboarding lead include a short runbook (endpoints, prefix caching, eval prompts to baseline quality).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
